The political reaction exposes the divisions in Giorgia Meloni’s ruling coalition. Matteo Salvini, leader of the far-right League, said the victory was “remarkable for the AdD” and reportedly sent a message of congratulations to its leader, Alice Wiedel. Antonio Tajani, who leads the centre-right Forza Italia, said the victory was “bad news” while Meloni, whose Brothers of Italy party has neofascist roots, has not said anything publicly. Some reports suggest her views align more with Tajani, in that the election result is not something to celebrate but should be a warning that the EU must be more effective in its response to the concerns of citizens. https://www.dw.com/en/polish-police-arre.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5PUfu Prefer DW on Google The three were arrested by security officials [FILE: October 2014] Image: Leszek Szymanski/EPA/dpa/picture alliance Advertisement Three teenagers have been arrested in Poland on suspicion of planning a terror attack , Tomasz Siemoniak, the minister in charge of Poland's special services, said in a post on social media on Monday. The suspects, a 16-year-old and two 17-year-olds, allegedly had links to an international neo-Nazi movement . The arrest comes days after a gunman with reported far-right leanings opened fire in Krakow, killing six people. What do we know about the suspected neo-Nazi terror plot? Siemoniak said in his post on X that the three teenagers had been arrested by the officials of the Internal Security Agency (ABW). "The teenagers not only promoted Nazi and fascist ideology but had already begun taking steps toward committing terrorist offenses," he said. During a search, ABW agents discovered chemicals used to make explosives, according to the minister. The suspects were also found to have exchanged information over messaging platforms on how to make explosives, firearms and pyrotechnics at home, with the intended use of carrying out a terror attack. The two 17-year-olds have been taken into pre-trial detention, with the 16-year-old being sent to a juvenile detention facility, Siemoniak said.
